entry.title:
New Anthropic Fellows research: Returning to the neuron basis for interpretability
Understanding wh...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces Fellows research revisiting neuron-level interpretability. The team re-examined three classic reasons the field abandoned neuron-based analysis (polysemantic neurons, concept drift across layers, distributed facts) by measuring each neuron's contribution to outputs rather than its activation triggers. All three problems proved smaller than assumed: neurons rarely combine unrelated concepts, outputs are semantically consistent across layers, and distributed facts remain readable.

entry.title: Launching Harness Comparisons on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index: the best harness varies...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a new Harness Comparisons feature on its Coding Agent Index, showing that agent harness choice significantly affects model performance and cost. Running GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3-Flash across 13 harnesses reveals no single best harness: GPT-6 Luna peaks in Codex while GLM-5.3-Flash peaks in Claude Code, and best performance-per-dollar harnesses differ per model.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Claude just claimed a proof of VP ≠ VNP, the 47-year-old algebraic version of P...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Reddit discussion, MTSlive explains that Anthropic posted a 70-page paper crediting Claude as sole author claiming a proof of VP not equal to VNP (Valiant's 47-year-old algebraic analogue of P vs NP) over every field, with both paper and Lean 4 formal proof written by AI models, verified by Lean's kernel plus an independent second checker nanoda; no human mathematician has yet checked it, and Anthropic says it does not settle P vs NP.

entry.title:
All intelligent systems I've ever seen have exactly two adaptation timescales.
The first one is on-...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet articulates a conceptual framework that intelligent systems have exactly two adaptation timescales: fast on-the-fly situation modeling (fluid intelligence, realized in modern AI via reasoning/program generation) and slow offline extraction of reusable abstractions from experience buffers (long-term plasticity, realized via pre-training and post-training). He argues that until late 2024, AI lacked the first timescale entirely, relying only on storage and retrieval of training-time patterns. The post references a slide from a recent Berkeley talk.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 23, 2026
entry.summary:
Governance dominated the day's discourse. Sam Altman unveiled OpenAI's transparency post proposing industry-wide shared development limits based on perplexity, with Greg Brockman endorsing it and framing around existing White House Accords commitments.

  • Yann LeCun went viral mocking superintelligence hype via the Level-5 driving gap, and separately downplayed AI bio-risk as overestimated
  • The claimed AI-assisted Riemann Hypothesis solution split opinion: Ethan Mollick showed top forecasters badly missed it, while Gary Marcus and LeCun credit the human mathematician over the model
  • François Chollet offered a contrarian economic take: deployment friction may actually benefit AI infrastructure by stretching the datacenter buildout
  • Tunguz ignited a heated legality debate, arguing distillation isn't illegal even on improperly obtained training data
  • Mollick also warned society may retreat from augmentation, and LeCun shared insider history on open-sourcing Llama-2
  • Jeremy Howard celebrated llms.txt adoption in Google Antigravity while critiquing Gemini-4-Neon coding agents for over-engineering

entry.summary: François Chollet argues to Musk and Tan that deployment friction in AI infrastructure may be beneficial: stretching the datacenter buildout over a longer timeline preserves pricing power and gives AI applications time to prove commercial viability, avoiding a capacity spike followed by a glut.

entry.summary: Expanding on yesterday's Reddit discussion, Mollick compiles predictions made just a month earlier about when the Riemann Hypothesis would be solved, contrasting Metaculus (May 2035), LEAP superforecasters (10% chance of another Millennium problem solved in 2026), and Terence Tao (humans plus AIs around 2050), implying recent events have outpaced them all.

entry.title: No distillation is illegal on stolen data.
entry.summary: Tunguz posts a pointed aphorism arguing that distillation itself is not illegal even when the underlying training data was obtained without authorization — a provocation in the debate over model distillation and data provenance.

entry.title:

He details how caching assumptions change for massive objects and release-day traffic floods.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 19, 2026
entry.summary:
A tense undercurrent ran through both: who controls frontier AI, and is it safe?

  • Demis Hassabis, Logan Kilpatrick, and Google DeepMind announced Neon as a frontier tier between Carbon and Hydrogen
  • Artificial Analysis independently ranked Neon #3 on its Intelligence Index (61) with strong cost-per-task coding results; François Chollet called its price-performance impressive
  • Anthropic's IPO drew an unprecedented safety backlash: the Center for AI Safety and EleutherAI co-founder Thom Wolf publicly signed a letter calling the lab unsafe
  • OpenAI disclosed exponential growth in researchers' AI use and recursive self-improvement indicators, plus up to 14% PPA chip-design gains with AMD in under five months
  • Expert commentary pushed back on hype: Sebastian Raschka likened benchmark comparisons to IQ tests for hiring; Chollet argued latent token demand is effectively infinite, constrained only by cost

Overall sentiment: excitement about Neon's price-performance and AI-accelerated silicon, deep division over Anthropic's accumulating power, and rising focus on AI improving AI itself.

entry.title: Google continues to accelerate its release cadence with Gemini 4 Neon, delivering a small Intelligen...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis provides a detailed breakdown of Google's newly released Gemini 4 Neon: it scores 61 on the Intelligence Index (1 point above Gemini 4 Carbon, 3rd overall behind GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2), costs ~17% less per task and ~40% less time per task than Carbon, and is Google's fourth model release in seven weeks.

entry.summary: Demis Hassabis announces the launch of Gemini 4 Neon, touting frontier-level intelligence, super fast task completion, and immediate availability to Pro and Ultra subscribers.

entry.title:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.
We find researchers' AI use contin...
entry.summary: OpenAI publishes new data on AI's role in its own research: researcher AI use is rising exponentially and agents complete longer tasks, while human effort on safety and alignment is growing fastest. OpenAI argues AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Working with @AMD, our models identified up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP in less than f...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports that in partnership with AMD its models achieved up to 14% power-performance-area improvement on flagship GPU IP in under five months, that the same approach improved OpenAI's custom Jalapeño inference chip with gains verified on real silicon, and announces work with Synopsys to bring model capabilities into EDA design and validation tools.

entry.summary: Thom Wolf explains why he signed an open letter critical of Anthropic: he argues Anthropic is on track to be the most powerful company on earth and therefore needs transparency near that of a sovereign government, while noting he disagrees with wording like reckless and mentions safety groups who felt unable to sign.

Massive engagement (~840K views, 11.4K likes).

entry.title: Social Summary: November 18, 2026
entry.summary:
Ethan Mollick found the model powerful yet hard to steer, Matt Shumer judged it below Anthropic's Claude, and Sam Altman conceded usability still needs work.

  • Demis Hassabis announced $5B for Isomorphic Labs, the day's biggest funding news, while Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas confirmed $1B ARR and launched Multiagent with Fable 5.2 orchestrating Gemini 4 Carbon and GPT-6.1 Sol
  • Agent architecture debates ran hot: Anthropic's Code Mode and a single-agent-beats-harnesses finding competed with Devin bot enthusiasm from swyx and Walden Yan
  • Open weights gained momentum: Clement Delangue shipped a Qwen coding-agent adaptation, Apple open-released FastFrames video models, and Mistral made Vibe free in Europe
  • Sebastian Raschka flagged a no-LR-decay pre-training trend, Jason Wei departed Meta for Mercor, and Gary Marcus warned of escalating infrastructure cyber attacks
